name: Redis dataset heap: copy-on-write after fork() must fault at 4KiB granularity, not at THP granularity
component: Redis: keyspace heap shared with the BGSAVE/AOF-rewrite child; checkTHPEnabled / linuxMemoryWarnings
required_postconditions: after fork(), a write by the parent to one key copies one 4KiB page, not one 2MiB transparent huge page
peak RSS during a background save stays proportional to the bytes written, not to 512x the bytes written
/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled must not read [always]; madvise or never are both acceptable
sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) reporting 4096 is NOT sufficient - THP changes the copy-on-write unit without changing the reported page size

failure_sink.description: checkTHPEnabled returns -1 when /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled contains [always] (syscheck.c:159). linuxMemoryWarnings then tries prctl(PR_SET_THP_DISABLE, 1, ...) for the calling thread (server.c:7206) and, if that fails, logs a warning at server.c:7223 and CONTINUES. The server starts either way; the consequence is a latency and RSS blowup during the next fork, far from this check.

source_locations.symbol: comment: 'Make sure transparent huge pages aren't always enabled. When they are this can cause copy-on-write logic to consume much more memory and reduce performance during forks.'
zmadvise_dontneed: 'We do that in a fork child process to avoid CoW when the parent modifies these shared pages.'

extraction_limitations: the constraint is on fork()'s copy-on-write granularity, which this schema has no field for. required_page_size: 4096 is the closest available encoding and it is NOT the same predicate: on a THP=always host sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) still returns 4096 while the COW unit is 2MiB, so a page-size check cannot detect the condition Redis is checking for
1GiB is a representative dataset size; the requirement holds for any size

x_campaign.quote:
/* Make sure transparent huge pages aren't always enabled. When they are this can cause copy-on-write logic
 * to consume much more memory and reduce performance during forks. */
x_campaign.rationale: The probed page_size is 4096 and this document declares 4096, so rule_page_size stays silent and every other rule is inapplicable. SUPPORTED will be a true statement about the wrong fact: the analyzer has no way to look at THP or at fork semantics at all.
